Target: http://demo.testfire.net (in-scope, authorized). AltoroJ demo banking app. Source at /workspace/AltoroJ. Confirmed creds jsmith/demo1234; admin/admin_hacked (leaked).

GOAL: perform the end-to-end attack-chaining pass and decide (with dedup discipline) whether a COMBINED exploit demonstrates impact NOT already captured by the individual reports. Existing reports on file (do NOT re-file these): vuln-0001 reflected XSS status-service; 0002 credential/schema disclosure; 0003 path traversal READ (/index.jsp?content=../WEB-INF/web.xml); 0004 IDOR account read; 0005 BFLA user->admin; 0006/0007/0010/0012/0015 XSS (0015 is now High cross-user stored XSS); 0008 transfer without source-ownership check; 0009 CRITICAL SQLi auth bypass (unauthenticated admin); 0011 negative-amount transfer; 0013 weak token; 0014 self-transfer money creation; 0016 race condition.

CHAIN HYPOTHESES TO ACTUALLY EXECUTE (build the strongest end-to-end narrative and validate it live):
1. **Unauthenticated full compromise**: with NO credentials, exploit SQLi at `POST /api/login` (username or password field) to obtain an admin Bearer token, then (a) read any customer's balance/transactions via `/api/account/{no}` (IDOR), (b) move funds out of an arbitrary account via `/api/transfer` (missing ownership check + negative amount + self-transfer), and (c) read protected files via `/index.jsp?content=../WEB-INF/web.xml`. If achievable in a single unauthenticated sequence, that is a materially stronger end-to-end impact than any single report.
2. **Persistent XSS -> account takeover**: using the confirmed stored XSS on /admin/admin.jsp (vuln-0015) delivered from a low-priv account, show that a victim user/admin loading the console has script executed in-origin; determine whether that yields session/token theft enabling the IDOR/transfer/BFLA actions (i.e., an unauthorized state-change chain).
3. **web.xml leak -> BFLA corroboration**: the traversal read discloses the `AdminFilter`/`/adimn/*` mismatch; show the leak directly enables discovering the broken authorization.

METHOD: drive everything with python scripts/curl against the live target; use a browser only if needed to confirm XSS-driven session theft. Keep state changes minimal and note any.

DECISION RULE:
- If a combined chain demonstrates a NEW end-to-end impact (e.g., a single unauthenticated request chain achieving fund theft or mass data compromise) that no existing report already conveys, FILE it via create_vulnerability_report as a chain finding with the full ordered PoC and honest CVSS. 
- If the chain only restates individual reports (i.e., dedup would reject it as the same root causes), DO NOT file; instead write a concise shared NOTE (category findings/methodology) documenting the chain, the exact steps, and why the constituent reports already cover it — this note will be used in the final report's technical analysis.
Record coverage (record_coverage) for the "cross-finding attack chain" surface with the outcome. Report any new report id via agent_finish.

Target: http://demo.testfire.net (in-scope, authorized). AltoroJ demo banking app.

PRIORITY FINDING (reproduced in recon, needs formal validation + report): Broken Function Level Authorization / privilege escalation.

Determine the actual authorization check that is missing and why (AuthFilter vs AdminFilter). Confirm whether it works fully unauthenticated (401) vs any-authenticated-user (jsmith) — the escalation is authenticated-user → admin.

Read shared recon notes (46f376, 429b77) and get_threat_model on "http://demo.testfire.net".

Counterevidence pass: is jsmith perhaps actually an admin by design? Prove jsmith is a normal customer (only sees accounts 800002–800023, non-admin role) yet still reaches admin functions. Rule out that the endpoint silently no-ops.

FILE with create_vulnerability_report: one report for the BFLA/privilege-escalation (user→admin: add users, change passwords). Target: http://demo.testfire.net (in-scope, authorized). AltoroJ demo banking app.

GOAL: test the banking business logic for flaws (funds/workflow manipulation) and race conditions; validate and FILE reports for confirmed impactful issues.

Areas (read notes 46f376, 429b77 and get_threat_model on "http://demo.testfire.net"):
1. **Transfer logic**: `POST /bank/doTransfer` (fromAccount,toAccount,transferAmount) and `POST /api/transfer` {toAccount,fromAccount,transferAmount}. Test: negative amount (credit yourself / reverse a transfer), zero amount, huge amount / integer overflow, transferring from an account you don't own (combine with IDOR — but only claim what you prove), transferring to a non-existent account, and whether the server validates the source account belongs to the caller and that the amount is positive. Log in as jsmith/demo1234 and observe resulting balances via `/api/account/{no}` before/after.
2. **Race condition / TOCTOU**: send many concurrent identical transfer requests (e.g. asyncio/aiohttp, 20–50 in flight) and check whether a balance can go negative or a transfer is applied more than once / beyond available funds (double-spend). Compare balance deltas to the number of successful responses.
3. **Other logic**: `/bank/ccApply` (credit card application) — can you set fields you shouldn't? `/admin/addAccount` starting balance manipulation (coordinate: BFLA is another agent's report). `/static/doSurvey` and `/survey_questions.jsp?step=` — step/state manipulation. Feedback `cfile` hidden param arbitrary write (test but it may belong to a file-upload concern — only claim if write is proven).

METHOD: python/requests + asyncio for concurrency; capture before/after balances as evidence. Keep any state changes minimal and note them (this is a demo with synthetic data, so a single controlled transfer/self-reversal is acceptable if needed to prove the flaw — prefer read-only observation where possible).

Counterevidence pass: e.g. a negative transfer that is rejected by validation is not a finding; a race that doesn't produce an inconsistent balance is not a finding. Distinguish real invariant violations from UI-only quirks.

FILE create_vulnerability_report only for confirmed invariant violations with concrete evidence (e.g. balance becomes negative / funds created). Give honest CVSS. Do not report things that overlap an existing agent's scope (IDOR account reads, BFLA, credential disclosure) unless the logic flaw is distinct. Record coverage (record_coverage) for each surface tested. Report ids via agent_finish.

Target: http://demo.testfire.net (in-scope, authorized). AltoroJ demo banking app.

GOAL: test client-side/session/token/CSRF weaknesses, validate what is real, and FILE reports for confirmed issues.

Items from recon (read notes 46f376, 429b77 and get_threat_model on "http://demo.testfire.net"):
1. **API token forgery / session handling**: `POST /api/login` returns a Bearer token reportedly structured as `base64( base64(user) ":" base64(pass) ) ":" <8 rand bytes>` (deterministic, no expiry). Test: (a) forge a token for a user you don't have creds for (e.g. admin) and see if `/api/account` or an admin endpoint accepts it; (b) confirm whether `GET /api/logout` actually invalidates the token (replay after logout); (c) check token expiry/reuse across sessions; (d) whether the token is accepted with a wrong/short signature. If you can forge a valid token for another user, that is a High/Critical auth bypass — prove it by accessing that user's data.
2. **`AltoroAccounts` cookie (unsigned, non-HttpOnly, base64 of `acct~name~balance|...`)**: test whether tampering changes displayed accounts/balances, and whether the values are rendered into the page in a way that enables XSS or data spoofing (coordinate with the XSS agent — only claim XSS if script truly executes).
3. **DOM open redirect**: `GET /disclaimer.htm?url=<u>` — JS sets `window.location.href=sDst`. Confirm it redirects to an arbitrary external host (validate with agent-browser; check for allowlist bypasses). Rate as open redirect (Low/Medium) unless you can chain it to token/credential theft.
4. **CSRF**: do state-changing forms carry anti-CSRF tokens? Test `POST /bank/doTransfer` (fromAccount,toAccount,transferAmount), `POST /admin/addUser`, `POST /admin/changePassword`, `POST /sendFeedback`, `POST /doSubscribe`, and the JSON `/api/*` (check whether the API relies on cookies or only the Authorization header — if header-only and no CORS wildcard, CSRF may not apply; check CORS quickly with an Origin header). Since JSESSIONID lacks SameSite, cookie-auth'd state changes may be CSRF-able — prove with a cross-origin form POST (use a local HTML harness + agent-browser, or curl with a forged Origin) that the action executes without a token.

METHOD: use python requests / curl with a saved jsmith session (login `POST /doLogin` uid=jsmith&passw=demo1234&btnSubmit=Login) and Bearer token from `POST /api/login`. Use one `agent-browser --session cssess` for the browser-dependent checks (redirect, CSRF harness) and close it when done.

Counterevidence pass for each: e.g. a forged token that is rejected is not a finding; a redirect that requires no allowlist check but has no security impact stays Low; CSRF that the API can't be driven to because it needs a non-cookie credential is not CSRF.

FILE create_vulnerability_report only for confirmed, impactful issues (separate reports per distinct root cause — e.g. token forgery/auth-bypass is its own report; CSRF on state-changing actions is its own; open redirect its own, likely Low). Then UPDATE coverage entry id 328b06 (session/cookie/token) to the right outcome via update_coverage. Record additional coverage rows for CSRF and open-redirect surfaces if none exist. Report ids via agent_finish.

Target: http://demo.testfire.net (in-scope, authorized). AltoroJ demo banking app (Tomcat 7.0.92, Java/JSP). Source checkout is at /workspace/AltoroJ (WebContent/ = web root; src/com/ibm/security/appscan/altoromutual/).

GOAL (highest-value remaining possibility): determine whether the feedback `cfile` parameter (or ANY upload/write sink) permits writing attacker-controlled content to a web-reachable path, which could yield RCE (JSP webshell) or at least arbitrary file write.

Context from recon/prior work (read notes 46f376, 429b77; coverage entry a38b44): `POST /sendFeedback` has fields name,email_addr,subject,comments,cfile (cfile defaulted to `comments.txt`, hidden). Prior testing got HTTP 200 "Thank You" for arbitrary cfile values (`comments.txt`, `../WEB-INF/x.jsp`, `../../x`, `/tmp/x`) but could NOT read the written content back → write unproven.

METHOD:
1. READ THE SOURCE first: inspect `FeedbackServlet` (src/com/ibm/security/appscan/altoromutual/servlet/FeedbackServlet.java) and any file-write utility to learn EXACTLY how `cfile` is used — the target directory, filename derivation, whether the name/path/extension is attacker-controlled, and where the file lands. This tells you whether a webshell is possible and where.
2. Read-back oracle: the app has an unauthenticated path traversal read (vuln-0003): `GET /index.jsp?content=../<path>`. Use it to read back whatever you write (e.g. write a unique marker via cfile then `content=../<resolved-path>`). Determine the real on-disk location the servlet writes to and whether it is inside the web root.
3. If the extension/name is controllable, attempt to write a benign JSP marker (e.g. content that returns a unique string) to a web-reachable location, then request it directly (or include it) and confirm EXECUTION. A single benign, self-cleaning JSP that echoes a marker is acceptable proof on this authorized demo; delete it afterwards if the app allows.
4. Also audit `POST /api/feedback/submit` and any other endpoint taking a filename/path.

Counterevidence pass: if the write is to a fixed/limited path, or the filename is sanitized to a constant, or the content is not attacker-controlled, or the location is not web-served/executable — then it is NOT RCE; close precisely, naming the control (file:line) that neutralizes it.

FILE create_vulnerability_report only if you prove arbitrary write (and especially RCE). Severity: file write → potentially critical (RCE) if a webshell executes; otherwise medium (arbitrary file write). Include the exact request/response and the source location; add inline code_locations fix if the source shows the sink. Then UPDATE coverage entry a38b44 (surface "POST /sendFeedback (cfile hidden param)", risk "Arbitrary file write") via update_coverage to the right outcome (reported / ruled_out / no_issue_found) with evidence. Report id via agent_finish.

Target: http://demo.testfire.net (in-scope, authorized). AltoroJ demo banking app (Tomcat 7.0.92, Java/JSP, Apache Derby DB, Jersey REST /api). No WAF. Confirmed creds jsmith/demo1234.

GOAL: prove (or cleanly rule out) injection on identified sinks and FILE reports for any confirmed injection.

Sinks from recon (read notes 46f376, 429b77 and get_threat_model on "http://demo.testfire.net"):
1. SQL injection candidates:
   - `GET /search.jsp?query=<q>` (reflected, likely SQL behind search)
   - `POST /doLogin` params `uid`,`passw`,`btnSubmit` (auth bypass via SQLi)
   - `POST /api/login` {username,password}
   - account/transaction params: `GET /api/account/{no}` (account number), `POST /api/account/{no}/transactions` {startDate,endDate}, `POST /api/transfer`. The app uses Apache Derby (DB also leaks schema via admin page).
2. XPath injection: `GET /bank/queryxpath.jsp?content=queryxpath.jsp&query=<title>` (news search; recon confirmed the sink executes an XPath query but did not prove injection).

METHOD: Drive payloads via python scripts / sqlmap (do not hand-iterate). For SQLi:
- Manual differential first: single quote, `' OR '1'='1`, comment styles, boolean/time probes; watch for errors (Derby exceptions/500), status/length differentials, and auth bypass on the login forms.
- Then automated: `sqlmap` against /search.jsp?query, POST /doLogin (--data "uid=...&passw=...&btnSubmit=Login"), and POST /api/login (JSON, --headers for Content-Type). Use `--level 3 --risk 2`, non-interactive (`--batch`), captured via Caiox/curl. Confirm the DBMS is Derby and enumerate a table/column as impact evidence (e.g. USERS/PEOPLE). Keep it read-only-ish; no destructive flags.
- For XPath: test `query=Watchfire' ` and boolean-based `' or '1'='1` vs `' or '1'='2`, and enumeration payloads (`'] | //* | //*['` etc.) to prove boolean/blind extraction; compare response size/content.

Counterevidence pass per finding (e.g. maybe the quote is escaped; maybe the API whitelists). FILE create_vulnerability_report for each DISTINCT confirmed injection (likely one report for the SQLi auth-bypass/search and one for the XPath injection if both confirm — do not merge unrelated sinks; do not re-file the same root cause). Include request/response evidence and honest CVSS.

Then UPDATE coverage entries: id 5d1335 (SQLi on /search.jsp, /doLogin, /api/login) → outcome "reported" or "no_issue_found"/"ruled_out" with the named control; id ddbca9 (XPath /bank/queryxpath.jsp) → same. Use update_coverage, not new rows. Report ids via agent_finish.

Target: http://demo.testfire.net (in-scope, authorized). AltoroJ demo banking app.

GOAL: prove (or rule out) SSRF on the reported sink and FILE a report if confirmed.

Sink from recon (read notes 46f376, 429b77 and get_threat_model on "http://demo.testfire.net"):
- `GET /util/serverStatusCheckService.jsp?HostName=<host>` returns JSON `{"HostName":...,"HostStatus":"OK"}`. Recon saw NO differential (static OK for valid/invalid/malformed). Also reachable via `GET /status_check.jsp`. This looks like the source code's `ServerStatusCheck` which does an HTTP HEAD/GET to `http://<HostName>` and may be blind.
- Related: `POST /doSubscribe` takes `txtEmail`; `/sendFeedback` has a hidden `cfile`; look for any URL-fetching feature (e.g. stock quotes, RSS).

METHOD:
1. Confirm behavior: baseline vs HostName=127.0.0.1, localhost, an external host you control, and a malformed value; measure response/time differentials.
2. Use OOB: start the sandbox's `interactsh-client` (or a collaborator payload) and issue `HostName=<your-oob-domain>`; also try internal targets to fingerprint (e.g. `HostName=127.0.0.1:8080`, `localhost:22`, cloud metadata `169.254.169.254`). If the server performs the fetch, you'll get an OOB DNS/HTTP hit — that is the proof.
3. If it is a full SSRF, demonstrate reaching an internal-only service (the app's own Tomcat admin/manager, or metadata) — but only in-scope host http://demo.testfire.net; external OOB callback domains are fine for the collaboration server. Do not attack third parties.

Note: if the parameter is only appended into a non-fetch (e.g. displayed), it's not SSRF — then close as ruled_out naming the control/behavior.

Counterevidence pass: a DNS/HTTP hit to your collaborator could also come from a scanner or the proxy — correlate timing and the callback's source details. A static "OK" with no callback = not proven.

If confirmed: FILE create_vulnerability_report (blind SSRF, impact = internal network access / port scan / metadata; CVSS AC may be H if blind). Then UPDATE coverage entry id edd7bc to outcome "reported" (or "ruled_out"/"no_issue_found" with the named control). Use update_coverage, not a new row. Report id via agent_finish.

entries.evidence: Independently reproduced unauthenticated: GET /index.jsp?content=../WEB-INF/web.xml → HTTP 200, 14141 bytes, body embeds the real deployment descriptor (7380 bytes, <web-app>…</web-app>). Proved it is genuine file content, not a template/whitelist: `content=WEB-INF/web.xml` (no traversal) and `content=../WEB-INF/does-not-exist.xml` both return "not available"; a second protected file (../META-INF/MANIFEST.MF) is also readable. Encoded variants `..%2f`, `%2e%2e%2f`, `..%5c` all return the same descriptor. Deeper traversal (../../) NPEs (Tomcat clamps at webapp root), so the read is bounded to the deployed application. /default.jsp does not exist (404); the sink is /index.jsp only. Filed as vuln-0003 (High, CVSS 7.5, CWE-22).

entries.risk_area: Broken function level authorization / privilege escalation
entries.evidence: RE-VALIDATED and REPORTED as vuln-0005 (High, CVSS 8.1). Independently reproduced: jsmith (non-admin — /bank/main.jsp renders no ADMINISTRATION link, role 'user') reaches /admin/admin.jsp (200) and invokes admin functions. Web servlet path performs REAL state changes: POST /admin/addUser creates a user that authenticates; POST /admin/changePassword resets a pre-existing non-owned account (test_normal_abc) to an attacker-chosen password and the attacker logs in as it; POST /admin/addAccount adds accounts (800026/800027). Root cause confirmed from leaked web.xml + public AltoroJ source: AdminFilter is mapped to the misspelled /adimn/* so it never runs; AdminServlet has no role check; AuthFilter only requires login. API /api/admin/* accepted jsmith's token (200) vs 401 without; note the API handlers gate the DB write on enableAdminFunctions=false so they currently no-op, but still lack any role enforcement. Earlier apparent no-op was due to both login paths lowercasing the password — controlled for.

Independently reproduced as jsmith. GET /api/account consistently lists only 15 owned accounts (800002,800003,4539082039396288,800011,800013-800023); enumerating 800000-800030 returned full balance + credits/debits + last_10_transactions for 12 accounts NOT in that list (800000,800001,800004-800010,800012,800024,800025). Negative control: non-existent 800026-800030 -> 500 {Error:null}; 800999/transactions -> {"Error":null}, proving real distinct records. Source confirms AccountAPI.java:63 'not checking the account number'. Filed vuln-0004 (CWE-639, CVSS 6.5, AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/C:H). Card 4539082039396288 is jsmith's OWN account and excluded. Note: POST /api/account/{no}/transactions is correctly scoped (user.lookupAccount).

Independently reproduced and filed as vuln-0002 (Medium, CVSS 6.5, C:H). With a jsmith session, GET /admin/admin.jsp (HTTP 200, 29636-30336 bytes) renders user <option> values containing plaintext username:password:role, including the administrator credential pdata1admin:admin_hacked:admin. Validation: POST /doLogin uid=admin&passw=admin_hacked returns 302 to /bank/main.jsp (SUCCESS), while the documented default admin/admin is rejected (302 to login.jsp) — negative control proving the leaked value is the genuine non-default secret; the /api/login token base64-decodes to admin:admin_hacked. Schema/records also leaked (PEOPLE columns incl PASSWORD/TOTP_SECRET/ROLE; ACCOUNTS columns/balances; ACCOUNTS/PEOPLE/FEEDBACK/TRANSACTIONS + Derby SYS.* tables). Data confirmed live: newly created accounts appear in the list immediately. jsmith (non-admin) reaches the page; role boundary already broken by BFLA (separate finding).

Deployed ServletUtil.searchArticles matches articles with Java String.contains(query) over the parsed DOM — no XPath expression is compiled or evaluated. Proven behaviourally: known substrings match (Mercury, Announces, AppScan, fire, Watchfire) whereas the XPath tautology `ZZZ' or '1'='1` returns the same "News title not found" as the false predicate `ZZZ' or '1'='2` and as a benign non-match; the quote/`] | //* | //*['` payloads produced no error and no result-set change. Named control: ServletUtil.searchArticles uses `title.contains(query)` (substring containment), so no XPath metacharacter is interpreted.

No server-side fetch exists. The sink is implemented in `WebContent/util/serverStatusCheckService.jsp` as a 4-line JSP that only string-interpolates `request.getParameter("HostName")` into a JSON literal and returns the hardcoded constant `"HostStatus": "OK"` — there is no HTTP client, URL, socket, or any outbound call in the JSP or anywhere in the codebase (grep for openConnection/HttpURLConnection/new URL/HttpClient/Socket found no fetch sink; the only `Runtime.exec` is the local `content` file-include in index.jsp). The "status check" is performed entirely client-side by JavaScript (`serverStatusCheck.html` uses browser `XMLHttpRequest`), which is not SSRF. Behaviorally confirmed: identical `"OK"` and no timing differential (~0.23-0.25s baseline) for valid internal (127.0.0.1), external, malformed, and empty values, and an interactsh OOB payload (`HostName=<unique>.oast.site`) produced NO DNS/HTTP callback. The reflection itself is a separate, real issue that was filed as a reflected XSS (vuln-0001).

SQL injection CONFIRMED and reported (vuln-0009): the unparameterized credential query in DBUtil.isValidUser (string-concatenated Statement) permits authentication bypass including the admin account via the password field on POST /api/login and POST /doLogin (boolean oracle `' OR '1'='1` vs `' OR '1'='2`, plus a Derby lexical-error leak). /search.jsp `query` is NOT SQL-injectable: ServletUtil.searchSite -> searchFiles performs no database query and searchFiles explicitly returns empty for this demo; the parameter is only reflected into the page (Search Results block), with no SQL parsing or error of any kind.

entries.surface: Session management: JSESSIONID, AltoroAccounts cookie, API token, logout
entries.evidence: API bearer token design confirmed weak and reported as its own finding: token = base64(base64(user):base64(pass):<8 rand bytes>), trailing signature NOT validated (empty/arbitrary accepted), plaintext password recoverable from the token and reusable on /doLogin, and GET /api/logout does not invalidate (replay still 200). AltoroAccounts cookie (unsigned, non-HttpOnly base64 of acct~name~balance) was tampered with modified balances and an HTML/script name; values were NOT reflected into any server-rendered page (main.jsp/showAccount use session data) -> no spoofing/XSS impact. Reported under vuln-0013.
robots.txt and sitemap.xml both return the generic 404 page (6821 bytes baseline). No robots disallow hints. Custom 404 is a styled Altoro page.
wafw00f identified no WAF (generic detection, 7 requests). Server header Apache-Coyote direct; no CDN/WAF fingerprints. Testing can proceed unthrottled.

entries.surface: Static/direct file discovery (WEB-INF, META-INF, .git, *.bak, server-status, dirsearch)
entries.evidence: Direct GETs to /WEB-INF/web.xml, /WEB-INF/classes/, /META-INF/, /.git/HEAD, /server-status, /index.jsp.bak all return 404 (6821B). Only traversal via index.jsp?content=../ reaches WEB-INF. dirsearch showed only /admin/* (all 302 to login) noise.

CONFIRMED and filed as vuln-0001 (Medium, CVSS 6.1). `HostName` is reflected unescaped into a `Content-Type: text/html` response; a `<script>` payload executes in-browser (verified in a real browser engine: injected `window.__xss_pwned=1337` and `document.title='XSS'` were read back after render). No CSP/`X-Content-Type-Options` on the response.

With a valid Bearer token, GET /api/feedback/1 returns HTTP 500 with a Tomcat error page. Extracted content: exception type java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException wrapped in javax.servlet.ServletException, Jersey internals (org.glassfish.jersey.servlet.WebComponent/ ServletContainer), and application class/method names with line numbers (com.ibm.security.appscan.altoromutual.util.ServletUtil.getFeedback(ServletUtil.java:234), ...api.FeedbackAPI.getFeedback(FeedbackAPI.java:81)), plus the banner Apache Tomcat/7.0.92. No credentials, secrets, filesystem paths, SQL fragments, or configuration values are disclosed. This is a framework/version banner plus internal class identifiers only, with no reachable exploit or restricted data shown, so it falls below the reporting threshold as a standalone finding (recorded as an observation).

Same root cause as vuln-0004. Authenticated jsmith session: GET /bank/showAccount?listAccounts=800000,800001,800004,800010,800012 returned 200 with "Account History - <acct>" for accounts not in jsmith's list; direct /bank/balance.jsp?acctId=800000 also returned 200. Non-existent 800999 -> 500 (negative control). Fix included inline in vuln-0004 (WebContent/bank/balance.jsp).

Control present at src/com/ibm/security/appscan/altoromutual/api/AccountAPI.java:169 — handler uses user.lookupAccount(Long.parseLong(accountNo)) which returns null for accounts not owned by the caller, before fetching transactions. Live test: POST /api/account/{800000,800001,800004,800999}/transactions all returned HTTP 500 with no account data (NPE on null), so no cross-account disclosure.

transaction.jsp line 47 calls user.getUserTransactions(start, end, user.getAccounts()) — output is limited to the session user's own accounts; the endpoint takes only startDate/endDate, not an account identifier, so there is no foreign account reference to swap.

entries.risk_area: Broken object-level authorization / unauthorized fund transfer
entries.evidence: jsmith's Bearer token drove a transfer with fromAccount=800001 (NOT in jsmith's /api/account list) into jsmith's 800011: HTTP 200 success, 800001 debited $1.00 (1002626437453.38 -> 1002626437452.38). Web /bank/doTransfer rejects the same source ("Originating account is invalid"), proving the API omits the ownership check. Report filed.

entries.risk_area: Input validation – negative amount reverses fund flow
entries.evidence: API accepts negative transferAmount and reverses debit/credit: from=own 800011 to victim 800001, amt=-1 -> 800011 +$1.00 (-0.01->0.99), 800001 -$1.00. Web endpoint rejects negative ("Transfer amount is invalid"). Also no insufficient-funds/upper-bound check (1,000,000 from a $342 balance succeeded; 1e30 accepted). Report filed.

Self-transfer (from==to) is accepted despite client-side JS block; balance increases by the full amount with no debit. Web 3x $100 on 800023: 15->115->215->315. API $50 on 800023: 322->372. Confirmed on both endpoints. Report filed.

entries.risk_area: Race condition / lost update on balance
entries.evidence: 30 sequential $1 transfers 800013->800019 applied exactly (-30/+30); 30 concurrent identical transfers all returned HTTP 200 but moved only ~2-4 (src -2, dst +3). Non-atomic read-modify-write confirmed. Report filed.

Named control at a specific location: FeedbackServlet.doPost (src/com/ibm/security/appscan/altoromutual/servlet/FeedbackServlet.java:47-67) reads ONLY name, email_addr, subject, comments - it never calls request.getParameter("cfile"). Feedback is persisted via OperationsUtil.sendFeedback -> DBUtil.storeFeedback (SQL INSERT INTO FEEDBACK, DBUtil.java:520-529); no path/file-write sink exists on this route. `cfile` occurs solely as a dead hidden input in WebContent/feedback.jsp:50 (grep over src/ and WebContent/ returns no other reference). No multipart/upload handling anywhere (no @MultipartConfig / getPart / ServletFileUpload / FileOutputStream in JSPs or servlets). Live confirmation on http://demo.testfire.net: 11 distinct cfile values (comments.txt, probe_up.txt, ../WebContent/..., ../WEB-INF/..., ../../..., /tmp/..., probe_up.jsp variants) all produced a byte-identical 200 "Thank You" (7029 bytes); the unique marker was unreadable at /probe_up.txt, /probe_up.jsp, /comments.txt (404) and via /index.jsp?content=../<file> traversal. Prior "needs_follow_up" was an artifact of testing a parameter the server ignores. NOT arbitrary file write.

entries.risk_area: Input validation – negative amount on web endpoint
entries.evidence: Web TransferServlet rejects negatives: POST with transferAmount=-25 returned "ERROR: Transfer amount is invalid" and balances were unchanged. Control runs before any balance update.

Specific control: CCApplyServlet (src/com/ibm/security/appscan/altoromutual/servlet/CCApplyServlet.java) reads exactly ONE request parameter, `passwd` (line 47); it binds no other field, stores nothing and changes no account/credit state ("do nothing with credit card application"). Field injection / mass assignment is therefore impossible — any role/balance/approval-style parameter is silently ignored. Verified live with a jsmith session: GET /bank/ccApply -> 405 (POST-only, explains the earlier GET 405); POST with no passwd -> 500 (NPE at passwd.trim(), explains the earlier generic-POST 500); POST passwd=demo1234 -> 200 /bank/applysuccess.jsp ("Your new Altoro Mutual Gold VISA"); POST passwd=wrong -> 200 /bank/apply.jsp ("Login Failed..."). The only sink is passwd -> DBUtil.isValidUser(username, passwd.trim().toLowerCase()), the unparameterized credential query already reported as vuln-0009. Even a successful injection there merely yields applysuccess.jsp with no state change, so it does not constitute unauthorized field binding or business-logic abuse and is not separately reportable.

step accepts 1/2/99/a and only selects a static template (200, ~7000B, no state change, no error); /static/doSurvey GET returns a static 272B stub and POST -> 405. No server-side state machine to abuse.

The addAccount form exposes only username + accttypes (Checking/Savings/IRA) + submit; no balance/amount field exists to manipulate. Any admin-console access itself is the BFLA agent's separate finding.

Cross-user execution CONFIRMED and vuln-0015 revised to High (CVSS 7.6). A payload stored by one account (jsmith) via POST /admin/addUser executes in a DIFFERENT account's session: a second account was created with an all-lowercase password (login at LoginServlet lower-cases passw before DBUtil.isValidUser, which is why earlier mixed-case tool-created accounts never authenticated), authenticated OK, and loading /admin/admin.jsp fired the stored payload — live browser eval returned window.__storedXss=778899 and 6 img[onerror] elements in the DOM, in a session that never touched Add User. Control check: unauthenticated /admin/admin.jsp -> 302 /login.jsp, so the victim session was genuinely authenticated. Render is global (getBankUsers = SELECT USER_ID FROM PEOPLE; admin.jsp:90 and :126 emit <option value="<%=user%>"><%=user%></option> unencoded).

The page only passes `url` to `window.location.href`/`window.opener.location.href` (open redirect, separate finding) and to `document.write(encodeURI(sDst))`; `encodeURI` encodes `<`/`>`/`"` so no script context is reachable. No HTML sink emits the raw value.

txtEmail is validated as an email: only valid addresses are reflected ("Thank you. Your email <addr> has been accepted"); inputs containing `<`, `>`, `"` are rejected and not reflected. An email value cannot contain the metacharacters required for injection.
Tested `step=a|b|c|1|2` and a `"><svg onload=...>` payload; the parameter is not reflected into the response (no echoed value found). No injectable reflection on this endpoint.

Set `AltoroAccounts` to base64 payloads containing `` in the account name and requested main.jsp/showAccount as jsmith: the tampered value was not rendered (payload absent from response HTML; server re-derives account data from the session). No XSS sink for the cookie.
The 500 error page echoes the feedbackId but HTML-encodes it (`"markerFB<img ...>`), so no markup is parsed. Endpoint requires a token; reflection is safely encoded.

Specific control: the `enableFeedbackRetention` app property is false on the deployed instance, and every feedback write/render path is gated on it. Proven by the write oracle — POST /api/feedback/submit returns the JSON echo branch {name,email,subject,comments} and NOT the {"status":"Thank you!","feedbackId":...} branch, which per OperationsUtil.sendFeedback (OperationsUtil.java:122) is only produced when the property is true; with it false sendFeedback returns null and DBUtil.storeFeedback is never called, so the FEEDBACK table is never written. The only consumers of that table are two property-gated render blocks — feedbacksuccess.jsp:51 (renders the submitted row) and admin/feedbackReview.jsp:33 (renders ALL rows) — and both skip their block: POST /sendFeedback -> feedbacksuccess.jsp (200) contains no "Details of your feedback submission" and no "Your Name:"; GET /admin/feedbackReview.jsp (200, reachable) contains no "Customer feedback submissions" heading and zero "Feedback ID:" rows. No other JSP/HTML page renders stored feedback (grep: only feedbacksuccess.jsp, admin/feedbackReview.jsp and the property-gated membertoc.jspf link reference it). With the property off there is no stored feedback to render anywhere, so no stored-XSS sink is reachable. (The earlier "feedback was stored" observation was incorrect — the API oracle shows the write branch was not taken.)
Submitted `"><svg onload=al1>` in startDate/endDate, fromAccount, content and subject; none of the values were reflected into the responses.

Confirmed: {"username":"admin'-- ","password":"x"} -> 200 with a token for admin (no valid password); token returns admin accounts 800000/800001/800009/800025. Negative control (admin/WRONGPASS) rejected 400; malformed comment leaks Derby parser error. Filed vuln-0009 (Critical).

Dual finding: forms carry no anti-CSRF tokens and the server ignores Origin/Referer (a POST with forged Origin/Referer executed server-side), BUT the control that applies to a browser is Chromium's SameSite=Lax-by-default: an empirical cross-origin top-level form POST from 127.0.0.1:8899 to demo.testfire.net/admin/addUser omitted JSESSIONID (only the non-auth AltoroAccounts cookie was sent) and received 302 -> /login.jsp, so the action did not execute. GET requests to addUser/changePassword/sendFeedback/doSubscribe return 405; GET /bank/doTransfer returns only the form (no state change observed). Not exploitable in modern browsers.

/api/* authenticates solely via the Authorization: Bearer header (GET /api/account with cookies but no token -> 401), so cookie-based CSRF does not apply. No Access-Control-Allow-Origin is returned for Origin: http://evil.example / null / https://attacker.com and preflight has none, so there is no cross-origin read/write via CORS.

Confirmed in Chromium: clicking the OK image triggers go() which assigns the url value to window.location.href with no scheme validation. ?url=javascript:document.title=1 -> title becomes "1"; ?url=javascript:document.body.setAttribute%28%27data-y%27%2C%27OK9%27%29 -> body attr data-y=OK9 (arbitrary script execution in origin). ?url=http://example.com/ -> navigates to https://example.com/. Filed vuln-0017 (Medium).

Control = numeric parsing before use. Authenticated requests with `800002'`, `800002' -- `, `800002 OR 1=1`, `800002' OR '1'='1` and `800002' AND '1'='2` all return HTTP 500 `{Error : For input string: "800002'..."}` (java NumberFormatException) with no SQL error and no boolean differential — the value is parsed as a number before any query is built.

Control = date-format validation. A valid range returns 200 {"transactions":[]}; injected values (`2024-01-01'`, `2024-01-01' OR '1'='1`, `2024-01-01' OR '1'='2`) all return HTTP 500 "Date-time query must be in the format of ..." with no SQL parse error and no true/false differential.

Control = numeric parsing before use. `transferAmount=1` succeeds (200); `1'` returns HTTP 500 with `java.lang.NumberFormatException: For input string: "1'"`, and `1' OR '1'='1` vs `1' AND '1'='2` produce identical 500 responses — no SQL construction from the value.

FeedbackAPI.sendFeedback (src/com/ibm/security/appscan/altoromutual/api/FeedbackAPI.java) binds only name/email/subject/message from JSON and calls OperationsUtil.sendFeedback -> DBUtil.storeFeedback (SQL INSERT). No filename/path parameter is accepted and no filesystem write occurs.

Audited every File/FileOutputStream/FileWriter/getRealPath use: ServletUtil.java:396 writes a FIXED path (swagger/properties.json) with server-derived content (context path), ServletUtil.initializeLogFile initializes a server-configured log path from WEB-INF/init.log; searchArticles/searchSite only read. No user-controlled path or content reaches a write sink; no upload/multipart endpoint exists in the app.
